subject: Export Compatibility & Redaction Matrix for Audit Exports
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Export requirements & redaction options - audit logs

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Acme's eDiscovery and forensic requirements we need clarification on Redwood's audit log export capabilities. Can you confirm the following?

- Supported export formats (NDJSON/CSV/Parquet) and whether each includes event metadata (timestamp, actor, request_id, model_version)
- Whether exports can be filtered by time-range, tenant-id, and route-id and produced incrementally
- Redaction options available during export: (a) none, (b) PII token-level redact, (c) schema-based field redaction
- Tamper-evidence: are exports accompanied by checksum/signature and do you provide a chain-of-custody manifest?
- Delivery methods: S3 presigned, SFTP, or direct streaming to a customer endpoint?

We also need a sample extract (a few hundred lines) and a short transfer playbook for procurement/legal review. Procurement is cc'd on this thread.

Appreciate a reply by EOD Friday — our internal timeline for the RFP requires draft evidence next week.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Security Operations
Acme Corp
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Export requirements & redaction options - audit logs

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a concise matrix and a small sample extract for your reviewers. Full playbook and SOP follow from Marissa.

- Formats: NDJSON (preferred), CSV (tabular summary), Parquet (columnar for analytics). NDJSON includes full event metadata (timestamp, actor id/email, request_id, model_version, route_id, region). CSV is a reduced view (no nested payloads).
- Filtering: yes. Exports support time-range, tenant-id, route-id, model_version, and severity. Incremental exports supported as delta snapshots (we can provide since/till tokens).
- Redaction modes: none; token-level redact (replace tokens with <REDACTED> while preserving token positions for sequence alignment); and schema-based redact (drop or mask predefined fields e.g., customer_email, user_message_text). We can also apply deterministic hashing for identifiers when required.
- Tamper-evidence: every export bundle is accompanied by a SHA-256 manifest and optional GPG signature. We maintain an audit manifest that records generation timestamp, export parameters, and the operator identity. Chain-of-custody template included in the SOP.
- Delivery: S3 presigned URL (preferred for large bundles), SFTP, or direct S3 to a customer-owned bucket (cross-account). For very large forensic snapshots we can arrange an encrypted physical transfer via partner channels.

Attachments: export_options_matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping format -> fields -> redaction capabilities) and sample_audit_excerpt.ndjson (~200 lines).

If you want, we can run a short export exercise against a synthetic/timestamped dataset so your legal team can validate redaction effectiveness.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-09-04T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Export requirements & redaction options - audit logs

Sean —

Thanks for the fast reply and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions from our security and eDiscovery teams:

1) For token-level redaction, can you demonstrate that alignment is preserved for auditing sequences? We need to be able to recompute request/response timelines without rehydrating content.
2) Does the NDJSON sample include request/response payloads by default? We are concerned about full user prompts and any PII present.
3) For cross-account S3 delivery, can Redwood push directly to an Acme bucket using an IAM role, or do you always use presigned URLs?

I've attached our evidence requirements doc (Acme_evidence_requirements.pdf) with the exact fields our downstream tools expect. Please confirm whether Redwood can deliver the named metadata and the recommended retention windows (30/90/365-day tiers) exposed in the matrix.

Daniel
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Export requirements & redaction options - audit logs

Hi Daniel — looping in a few details and the transfer SOP. We can accommodate the items in your requirements doc; summary and operational notes below. Attachment: evidence_transfer_sop.md

Operational summary:
- Token-level redaction: yes — we preserve token indexes in the export. That allows timelines and sequence alignment (hashes of token positions included). We will provide a short test harness so your engineering team can validate alignment on the synthetic sample.
- NDJSON payloads: configurable. By default NDJSON includes full request/response objects (useful for debugging), but for evidence deliveries we can apply a redaction profile to strip or mask prompt_text and output_text fields. We can also emit a metadata-only NDJSON.
- Cross-account S3: we support two modes: (1) presigned URLs (push model), (2) we can write directly to your S3 bucket using a short-lived cross-account role that you grant (preferred for automation). We do not retain credentials.
- Retention tiers: Redwood supports configurable retention per-tenant: 30 days (default), 90 days, 365 days, or custom policies via the console or API. Exports can be backfilled for older windows subject to export SLA.

Next steps we propose:
1) Run a 1-hour sandbox export with token-level redaction applied to verify alignment (we'll use synthetic data).
2) Agree on delivery method (S3 role vs presigned).
3) Sign off on the export manifest template and chain-of-custody fields.

If acceptable, Sean and I will schedule the sandbox for next Tuesday and provision the playbook.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: Export requirements & redaction options - audit logs

Daniel —

Thanks — confirming next steps and timeline so procurement/legal have a single plan to review: 

- Sandbox export: provisioned Tue 2026-09-14 (1-hour window). Deliverables: token-redacted NDJSON sample, metadata-only NDJSON, CSV summary.
- Delivery method: please confirm if you prefer cross-account IAM role or presigned URL. If role, share the role ARN and we'll perform a single-role-assume write test.
- Manifest & CoC: we'll provide the SHA-256 manifest, GPG signature (optional), and a chain-of-custody template we use in similar engagements (link below).
- Retention confirmation: Redwood will apply tenant-level retention per the RFP once contracted. Backfill exports for historical windows can be scheduled (timeline depends on window size; typical 24–48h for up to 90 days).

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_acme-audit-deliverables (playbook + manifest template), HubSpot: 678912

If procurement wants the sample transferred to a staging S3 this week for validation, let me know and we'll arrange it with minimal data (synthetic). Otherwise we'll proceed with the sandbox next week.

Action items for Acme: confirm delivery method (S3 role ARN or presigned) and provide a preferred test bucket or confirm we should use presigned links.
